It's 20p for 500g of their own brand of dry spaghetti here (UK) penne is 29p, and branded pasta including fusili and other shapes starts at about 40p. What's it like where you are? 

Ways I save money on food include not eating meat (I don't like it that much so it's not just for money saving reasons but don't worry I still get protein from eggs, beans, and Quorn), cooking all meals from scratch, not eating out or ordering food (I've had one takeaway this year and even then I just ordered the curry and cooked my own rice), not really buying snacks (I get the occasional pack of 44p chocolate bourbon biscuits or sometimes bake my own cookies) and I only drink tea and water bc that's what I like, I don't even get milk

The way I eat definitely does not suit other people for sure, but I am really interested in cooking my own food and doing it for as cheap as possible while keeping it interesting and flavorful. I do repeat a lot of meals but that's the cost for me of eating cheap

I really am quite small at 5'1 and 50kg, don't exercise or socialise outside of home/work much so I think that also contributes to my spending habits. 

Also £40 is about 52$ according to google

Why are they waiting? Think of how much change they could bring the world now. Honestly just sounds like a pr stunt to say they're gonna do this when they die, when they could do it now and help people now.

I'm just asking why they're waiting to give away 90 billion dollars when the world really could do with it already, think of how it could be invested in reducing the effects of climate change or ending world hunger

And what's the point of telling us now that they're going to do it when they die it's like oh yay this money that could help the world so much can't be used until these people die in 20 ish years

And that's not even guaranteed like who's going to check that they're doing that? 

Just seems like they're trying to pat themselves on the shoulder for making this huge promise. It's not enough to make a promise for the future like that, it should just be done now, and if it was it could prevent so many bad things whereas if they wait to donate the world may have gotten much worse by then and their money won't make as much of a difference.

I'm not saying they're bad people don't get me wrong, just wondering what's stopping them from helping humanity now.
